subject: Oceanography
title: Surface Currents
description: A short lesson to help you apply Surface Currents.

hook.text: Wind drags the ocean surface into vast rivers of water that stretch across entire ocean basins.

buildup.text: Trade winds and westerlies push surface water into circular patterns called gyres.

discovery.text: Five major gyres exist—each spinning clockwise in the north, counterclockwise in the south.

twist.text: The Coriolis effect (Earth's rotation) deflects moving water, shaping the curves of every gyre.

climax.text: Surface currents redistribute heat from the tropics to the poles, moderating global climate.

punchline.text: Wind and spin drive rivers within the sea.

quiz.question: What primarily drives surface ocean currents?
